## Scientific Balloon Solutions

https://www.scientificballoonsolutions.com/products/

I have one SBS-13 that was provided to me. 

specs from SBS website:

> New SBS-13 Version 2 is a machine seamed Super Pressure Balloon.
> Estimated Altitude (43k-45k feet)  (13.1km -13.7km)
> Dimensions when flat on table (3’ W X 7.5’ L)  (0.91m W X 2.28m L)
> Film Thickness, (1mil) Pic

They do not list the inflated dimension or the mass. I made my own measurements shown in @fig-sbs-13-dims. 

![SBS-13 dimensions as measured](/_sources/balloons/sbs-13-dims.jpg){#fig-sbs-13-dims)

I modeled it as a cylinder with two hemispherical end caps. 

- Cylinder center: 107-110 cm long, circumference 186 cm
- End caps: half-circumference 125-134 cm
- Mass: 105 grams


### Determine the volume

```{python}
#| label: sbs-13-volume

import numpy as np

# cylinder section
length = 110.0 # cm
circumference = 186.0 # cm
radius = circumference / (2*np.pi) # cm
volume_cyl = np.pi * radius**2 * length # cm**3

# end caps
half_circumference = 130.0 # cm
full_circumference = half_circumference * 2.0 # cm
radius = circumference / (2*np.pi) # cm
volume_end = 4.0/3.0 * np.pi * radius**3 # cm**3
# there are two end caps, so it's like a full sphere

# total volume
volume_total = volume_cyl + volume_end # cm**3

# total volume in m**3
volume_total_cubic_meter = volume_total/100**3

print(f'Total volume: {volume_total_cubic_meter}')
```

Total volume: 0.411 cubic meter
